## Highlights

- Chat can use OpenAI's GPT-6 models. GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6 Sol, GPT-6 Luna and GPT-6.1 Sol are
  offered through an OpenAI API key or environment-variable credential, and Tale calls Astra and
  GPT-6.1 Sol through the Responses API, the only way they make tool calls. Project agents and
  automations run those two on Codex; another runtime now says so instead of refusing without a
  reason. Subscription credentials are marked **Tasks and automations only** in Settings, and the
  chat model list names the subscriptions it leaves out.
  [Run the GPT-6 models](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/admin/providers#run-the-gpt-6-models)
  · [#4181](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4181)
- A standing task that stays in **Backlog** or **To do** while its agent works is retried
  automatically after a retryable failure, as long as its status, assignee, archive state and
  review stay unchanged. Before, the task kept reporting a pending retry and held an idle agent.
  [Triggers](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/automations/triggers)
  · [#4187](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4187)
- A workflow step whose sandbox workspace is being destroyed now fails at once with the reason,
  instead of waiting up to two hours for room and then running in a fresh, empty workspace.
  [Sandboxes](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/admin/sandboxes)
  · [#4144](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4144)
- A data-subject erasure completes only once the sandbox service confirms that the person's agent
  workspaces are deleted. Until then its receipt reads **Partial**, and **Retry** finishes it
  later. The audit log's **Sandbox workspace deleted** event also waits for that confirmation.
  [Data subject requests](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/admin/governance/data-subject-requests)
  · [#4094](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4094)
- Sandboxes hold up better under sustained load. They release finished command output,
  disconnected readers and stalled streams, cap held-open input at 8 MiB, rotate the logs of
  nested Docker containers, replay long runs faster and no longer repeat cleanup work that used
  CPU. A package-cache volume deleted shortly after it was prepared comes back writable, so
  package installs no longer fail with permission errors.
  [#4174](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4174),
  [#4182](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4182),
  [#4184](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4184),
  [#4185](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4185),
  [#4188](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4188),
  [#4154](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4154)
- The sandbox runtime updates all nine bundled agent runtimes (Claude Code 2.1.285, Codex 0.160.0,
  Cursor 2026.10.01, Gemini CLI 0.62.0, Hermes 0.19.0, OpenClaw 2026.9.8, OpenCode 1.18.34,
  Pi 1.0.1 and Qwen Code 0.24.7) on Node 24.21.0. Qwen Code no longer starts the Playwright MCP
  server on every turn; the server starts with the first browser tool call.
  [Harnesses](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/agents/harnesses)
  · [#4140](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4140)
- Fixes you can see in the app:
  - **Add credential** shows a loading state while the provider or connector catalog loads,
    instead of reporting that the deployment ships no provider files.
    [#4161](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4161)
  - Home drops a deleted or archived project's tasks and chats without a reload
    ([#4162](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4162)), and shows the **Draft** badge for
    a draft of literal code such as `<Button />`
    ([#4204](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4204)).
  - Comments written by automations are labelled as automation instead of "Deleted agent".
    [#4164](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4164)
  - A recorded approval decision no longer answers with an error when waking the run fails
    afterwards, and the approval card offers **Try again** when the approval cannot be loaded or
    keeps **Approve** and **Reject** when a decision was not recorded.
    [Approvals in workflows](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/automations/approvals-in-workflows)
    · [#3881](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/3881)
  - Adding teams to a project's audience one after another keeps every team
    ([#4197](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4197)), and a renamed team shows its new
    name in the open detail panel and editor
    ([#4193](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4193)).
  - Product **Create** stays disabled while the product is saved, so a repeated click cannot send
    a second request ([#4198](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4198)), and the product
    list formats prices in the reader's locale
    ([#4205](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4205)).
  - A queued or failed outbound mail and a chat message keep the attachment bytes they list, so
    deleting the file no longer breaks the send or a later chat turn.
    [#4157](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4157)
  - A website's scan-failure alert no longer comes and goes with the page filter
    ([#4135](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4135)), and the arrow, Home and End keys
    select the focused option of a segmented control such as that filter
    ([#4163](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4163)).
- The front pages of the website, the documentation and the UI documentation are reworked, and
  the pricing table names the data processing agreement as the service only Enterprise includes.
  [#4139](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4139),
  [#4148](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4148)
- Operators can sample backend HTTP and worker spans through the existing Sentry integration. It
  is off by default.
  [Observability](https://docs.tale.dev/self-hosted/configuration/observability-config)

## Upgrade notes

- The backend applies database migration `0149` when it starts. It adds the state that standing
  task retries need and an index on task activity, and it retires the pending retries of failed
  standing-task runs from earlier versions without starting catch-up work; their history stays.
  Building the index can lengthen the first start on an instance with a long task history.
- Two optional environment variables, documented in the
  [environment reference](https://docs.tale.dev/self-hosted/configuration/environment-reference),
  change nothing until you set them:
  - `SANDBOX_DOCKER_WORKLOADS` limits which workloads may start Docker inside the sandbox when
    the deployment enables it. The default, `project,workflow`, keeps today's behavior; `project`
    runs workflow agents without Docker. It applies to sessions created afterwards. The
    repository's `compose.yml` and `tale deploy` pass it to the sandbox service; a hand-written
    Compose file or manifest must pass it as well.
  - `BACKEND_SENTRY_TRACES_SAMPLE_RATE`, `0` by default, samples backend HTTP and worker spans.
    It needs `SENTRY_DSN` and a destination that accepts Sentry transactions. Recreate the
    backend API and worker services after changing it.
- Without an explicit `SANDBOX_AGENT_MEMORY`, a sandbox session without Docker inside now
  defaults to `4g` of memory and a session with Docker to `8g`, even when other sessions in the
  deployment use Docker.
- The sandbox runtime image grows to about 6.0 GB on amd64 with the refreshed agent runtimes.
  Allow for the larger pull and disk use.
- Update the sandbox service and connected sandbox devices together with the platform. Older
  versions cannot confirm workspace deletion, so erasure receipts remain **Partial** until those
  services and devices are updated; retrying alone cannot fix the missing confirmation.
- On Kubernetes, sandbox Pods that are still Pending count against admission, and maintenance
  removes a Pod left Pending past its startup deadline plus 60 seconds while keeping its
  workspace volume. A deleted workspace counts as erased once its volume is handed to the storage
  provisioner; with a `Retain` reclaim policy, its files stay until you remove the volume.
  [Kubernetes](https://docs.tale.dev/self-hosted/install/kubernetes)
- Known limitations: bytes that a queued mail or a chat message keeps are not removed when that
  mail or chat ends, and a chat attachment can keep a document's bytes after a retention
  destruction ([#4208](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4208)). GPT-6 models in chat
  do not carry their reasoning across tool rounds within a turn.
- The API contract stays at 3.15.0.
